guides.title: Make Text Bigger
guides.description: Make the letters on your screen larger so they are easier to read.

verification.applies_to: iPhone with a recent iOS. iPhone 15, 16 and 17 use the same path.

steps.text: Open the Settings app.
steps.image_alt: Settings app icon on the Home screen

steps.text: Tap Display & Brightness.
Tap Text Size.
Drag the slider to the right to make the text bigger.

tips: Need it even bigger? Go to Settings > Accessibility > Display & Text Size > Larger Text, turn on Larger Accessibility Sizes, then drag the slider.
For thicker, clearer letters, go to Settings > Accessibility > Display & Text Size and turn on Bold Text.
A few apps ignore this setting. Look inside the app for its own text size option.

verification.applies_to: General Android. Menu names differ by brand. Used only when no brand guide exists.

steps.text: Open the Settings app.
Look for Display or Display & Brightness and open it.
Look for Font Size or Text Size.
Choose a larger text size.

verification.applies_to: Windows 11

steps.text: Press the Windows key and the letter U together. This opens Accessibility settings. (Or click Start, then Settings, then Accessibility.)
steps.image_alt: Settings app icon on the Home screen

steps.text: Click Text size.
Drag the Text size slider to the right to make letters bigger.
steps.image_alt: Text size slider with preview box

steps.text: Click Apply.

tips: This changes only the text. To make pictures, buttons and everything else bigger too, go to Settings > System > Display and raise the Scale percentage.
Pressing the Windows key and the plus (+) key opens Magnifier for a quick zoom.

verification.applies_to: Recent macOS that has the Text size option under Accessibility > Display (Sequoia or newer). Older versions may not have it.

steps.text: Click the Apple icon in the top-left corner of the screen, then click System Settings.
Click Accessibility in the left-hand list.
Click Display.
Find Text size and choose a bigger size.

tips: Not every app follows this. Some apps have their own text size setting.
To make everything bigger: System Settings > Displays, then choose a Larger Text option (on Apple screens) or a lower resolution.

verification.applies_to: Galaxy phones on One UI. Samsung says screens vary by software version and model.

steps.text: Open the Settings app.
Tap Display.
Tap Font size and style.
Drag the Font size slider to the right to make the text bigger.

tips: Turn on Bold font on the same screen for thicker letters.
To make icons and everything else bigger too, go back to Display and tap Screen zoom.

verification.applies_to: Xiaomi, Redmi and POCO on MIUI or HyperOS. No official Xiaomi page was found for this task. Menu names may differ on newer HyperOS.

steps.text: Open the Settings app.
Tap Display.
Tap Text size.
Choose a bigger size.

tips: If you cannot find it, tap the search box at the top of Settings and type: font
If the biggest size is still too small, search Settings for Display size to make icons and text bigger together.

verification.applies_to: OPPO phones on ColorOS. No official OPPO page was found for this task. Menu names may differ by ColorOS version.

steps.text: Open the Settings app.
Tap Display & brightness.
Tap Font & display size.
Drag the Font size slider to the right, then tap Apply.
steps.image_alt: Font size slider and Apply button

tips: The Display size slider on the same screen makes icons and menus bigger too.
If you cannot find it, tap the search box at the top of Settings and type: font

guides.title: Take a Screenshot
guides.description: Save a picture of what is on your screen, for example a message or a bill.

verification.applies_to: iPhones with Face ID (no Home button). iPhone 15, 16 and 17 all qualify. On iOS 26 the screenshot may open full screen afterwards; that detail comes from a third-party page.

steps.text: Open the screen you want to save.
steps.image_alt: Any screen you want to capture

steps.text: Press the Side button (right edge) and the Volume Up button (upper button on the left edge) at the same time.
steps.image_alt: Side button and Volume Up button highlighted

steps.text: Let go quickly. The screen flashes and a small preview appears. Your screenshot is saved in the Photos app.
steps.image_alt: Screenshot preview in the lower-left corner

tips: To find it later: open Photos, scroll down to Media Types, then tap Screenshots.
On iOS 26 the screenshot may open full screen. Tap the tick or Done and choose Save to Photos.
Press and release quickly. Holding the buttons down does something else.

verification.applies_to: Most Android phones. Used only when no brand guide exists.

steps.text: Open the screen you want to save.
steps.image_alt: Any screen you want to capture

steps.text: Press the Power button and the Volume Down button at the same time.
steps.image_alt: Power and Volume Down buttons highlighted

steps.text: The screen flashes. Your screenshot is saved in your Gallery or Photos app.

verification.applies_to: Windows 11. The Windows + Shift + S shortcut also appears in a copy of Microsoft's own Snipping Tool article, but the official page itself was not opened.

steps.text: Open the screen you want to save.
steps.image_alt: Any screen you want to capture

steps.text: Press the Windows key, the Shift key and the letter S together.
steps.image_alt: Windows, Shift and S keys highlighted

steps.text: The screen goes dark. Click and drag over the part you want to keep.
steps.image_alt: Dimmed screen with a selection rectangle

steps.text: The picture is copied. To use it, open an email or document and press Ctrl and V together to paste it.
If you don't want to do all these steps you can search for Snipping Tool in the Start menu and can do step 3.
To save the screenshot as a file, click the notification that appears after step 4. Then click the Save icon and choose where to save it.

tips: To save the whole screen as a file instead, press the Windows key and the Print Screen key (PrtSc). It goes into Pictures > Screenshots.

verification.applies_to: MacBook Air and MacBook Pro on current macOS.

steps.text: To save the whole screen, press Shift, Command and 3 together.
To save only part of the screen, press Shift, Command and 4 together, then click and drag over the part you want.
steps.image_alt: Crosshair selecting part of the screen

steps.text: By default the picture is saved on your Desktop. A small preview may also appear in the corner of the screen.

tips: Shift, Command and 5 opens the Screenshot app with buttons for everything, including screen recording.
Add the Control key to copy the picture instead of saving it, for example Control, Shift, Command and 3.

verification.applies_to: Galaxy phones and tablets. Samsung says button positions can vary slightly by model.

steps.text: Open the screen you want to save.
steps.image_alt: Any screen you want to capture

steps.text: Press the Side (power) button and the Volume Down button together, then let go after a moment.
steps.image_alt: Side button and Volume Down button highlighted

steps.text: The screen flashes. Your screenshot is saved in the Gallery app.

tips: Press briefly. Holding the Side button too long opens the power menu instead.
Most Galaxy phones also let you swipe the edge of your hand across the screen (palm swipe). It may need to be switched on in Settings.

verification.applies_to: Xiaomi and Redmi phones. Xiaomi's pages cover Redmi 12 and 13C; the three models in this app were not individually checked.

steps.text: Open the screen you want to save.
steps.image_alt: Any screen you want to capture

steps.text: Swipe down from the top-right corner of the screen to open Control Center.
Tap Screenshot.

tips: To use the buttons or a three-finger swipe instead: Settings > Additional settings > Gesture shortcuts > Take a screenshot. Then choose Slide 3 fingers down or Volume down + Power.
Not every Redmi model can take a long (scrolling) screenshot. Xiaomi says the Redmi 13C cannot.

verification.applies_to: OPPO phones on ColorOS. The gesture menu path depends on the ColorOS version.

steps.text: Open the screen you want to save.
steps.image_alt: Any screen you want to capture

steps.text: Press and hold the Power button and the Volume Down button together for about 2 seconds.
steps.image_alt: Power and Volume Down buttons highlighted

steps.text: The screen flashes white. Your screenshot is saved.

tips: To use a three-finger swipe down: on ColorOS 15 or newer go to Settings > Accessibility & convenience > Screenshot and turn on 3-finger swipe down. On ColorOS 13 or 14 go to Settings > Additional Settings > Screenshot.

verification.applies_to: Windows 11. The Windows + Shift + S shortcut also appears in a copy of Microsoft's own Snipping Tool article, but the official page itself was not opened.

steps.image_alt: Windows, Shift and S keys highlighted

steps.image_alt: Dimmed screen with a selection rectangle

If you don't want to do all these steps you can search for Snipping Tool in the Start menu and can do step 3.
To save the screenshot as a file, click the notification that appears after step 4. Then click the Save icon and choose where to save it.

tips: To save the whole screen as a file instead, press the Windows key and the Print Screen key (PrtSc). It goes into Pictures > Screenshots.

guides.title: Turn On the Flashlight
guides.description: Use your phone's built-in torch in the dark.

verification.applies_to: iPhones with Face ID (iPhone 15, 16, 17).

steps.text: Swipe down from the top-right corner of the screen to open Control Center.
Tap the Flashlight button (it looks like a torch).
To turn it off, tap the same button again.

tips: If you do not see the Flashlight button, go to Settings > Control Center and add Flashlight.
On the Lock Screen there may be a flashlight button at the bottom. Press and hold it to turn the light on or off.

verification.applies_to: General Android steps, used for Xiaomi and OPPO until their own pages are checked.

steps.text: Swipe down from the top of the screen to open the quick settings panel.
Look for the Flashlight icon. If you cannot see it, swipe left or right on the panel.
Tap the Flashlight icon. Tap it again to turn the light off.

verification.applies_to: Galaxy phones. The icon may be on a second page of the panel.

steps.text: Swipe down from the top of the screen with two fingers to open the Quick settings panel.
Find the Flashlight icon. If you cannot see it, swipe right on the panel.
Tap the Flashlight icon to turn it on. Tap it again to turn it off.

tips: Press and hold the Flashlight icon to change how bright it is.

guides.title: Connect to Wi-Fi
guides.description: Join your home Wi-Fi so you can use the internet without using mobile data.

verification.applies_to: iPhone with a recent iOS.

steps.text: Open the Settings app.
Tap Wi-Fi.
steps.image_alt: Wi-Fi row at the top of Settings

steps.text: Make sure the Wi-Fi switch at the top is turned on.
Tap the name of your Wi-Fi network in the list.
If it asks, type the Wi-Fi password and tap Join. A blue tick next to the name means you are connected.
steps.image_alt: Password box and blue tick next to the network

tips: The Wi-Fi password is usually printed on a sticker on the router.
Never share a Wi-Fi password with a stranger who calls you.

verification.applies_to: General Android steps, used for Xiaomi and OPPO until their own pages are checked. On some phones this is called WLAN.

steps.text: Open the Settings app.
Tap Wi-Fi. On some phones this may be called WLAN or be inside Network & internet.
Turn the Wi-Fi switch on.
Tap the name of your Wi-Fi network.
Type the Wi-Fi password and tap Connect.

tips: The Wi-Fi password is usually printed on a sticker on the router.

verification.applies_to: Windows 11

steps.text: Click the small icons (Wi-Fi, speaker, battery) at the bottom-right corner of the screen.
steps.image_alt: Network, sound and battery icons in the taskbar

steps.text: Click the small arrow next to the Wi-Fi button to see the list of networks and turn on the Wi-Fi.
steps.image_alt: Arrow next to the Wi-Fi button

steps.text: Click the name of your Wi-Fi network, then click Connect.
Type the Wi-Fi password and click Next. When it says Connected, you are done.

tips: If the Wi-Fi button is grey, click the button itself once to turn Wi-Fi on.
The Wi-Fi password is usually printed on a sticker on the router.

verification.applies_to: Galaxy phones.

steps.text: Open the Settings app.
Tap Connections.
Tap Wi-Fi, and turn it on if it is off.
Tap the name of your Wi-Fi network.
Type the Wi-Fi password and tap Connect.
You can swipe down and click on Wi-Fi directly too and then follow steps 4 and 5.

tips: You can also swipe down from the top with two fingers and tap the Wi-Fi icon to turn Wi-Fi on quickly.
The Wi-Fi password is usually printed on a sticker on the router.

guides.title: Make a WhatsApp Video Call
guides.description: See and talk to family and friends on a video call using WhatsApp.

verification.applies_to: WhatsApp on iPhone. The first three steps come from WhatsApp's help page; the permissions tip comes from a third-party page.

steps.text: Open the WhatsApp app.
Tap the chat with the person you want to call.
steps.image_alt: Chat list with one chat highlighted

steps.text: Tap the video camera icon at the top of the chat.
steps.image_alt: Video camera icon at the top of the chat

steps.text: If WhatsApp asks to use the camera or microphone, tap Allow. Wait for the other person to answer.

tips: If the camera or sound does not work: open Settings, scroll down to WhatsApp, and turn on Camera and Microphone.
A video call uses a lot of internet. Joining Wi-Fi first saves your mobile data.

verification.applies_to: WhatsApp on any Android phone (Samsung, Xiaomi, OPPO). The first three steps come from WhatsApp's help page; the permissions tip comes from a third-party page.

steps.text: Open the WhatsApp app.
Tap the chat with the person you want to call.
steps.image_alt: Chat list with one chat highlighted

steps.text: Tap the video camera icon at the top of the chat. If it asks you to confirm, tap Call.
steps.image_alt: Video camera icon at the top of the chat

steps.text: If WhatsApp asks to use the camera or microphone, tap Allow. Wait for the other person to answer.

tips: If the camera or sound does not work: open Settings > Apps > WhatsApp > Permissions and allow Camera and Microphone.
A video call uses a lot of internet. Joining Wi-Fi first saves your mobile data.
